title: The School Says Your Teen Missed Class. They Left Home This Morning. What Now?
summary: A safety-first response to an absence alert: locate your teen, check the exact attendance mark, hear their account, and agree the next school-day step.
seo_title: Teen Missed Class? What Parents Do First
seo_description: Your teen left home, but school says they missed class. Locate them first, check the attendance record, then talk privately and plan one school-day step.
release_move: The parent verifies location, safety, and the attendance record; once safe, the teen can own one feasible school contact or catch-up action with a check-in time.

core_belief_shift.from: A missed-class alert proves my teen skipped or the school made a mistake; I should confront one of them immediately.
core_belief_shift.to: I should establish safety, verify the exact attendance facts, then hear my teen and agree a proportionate next step.

book_relevance.reason: The War Playbook Chapter 1, Don't Fight Blind, supports checking incomplete facts before a charged response only after immediate location and safety duties. Social Chapter 7 and Discipline Chapter 1 are narrower optional listening and next-action connections.

hero.alt: A concerned father checks his phone as his teenage daughter arrives safely home with her school bag; they pause to talk at the doorway.

social_image.alt: A concerned father sees that his teenage daughter is safely home after an attendance alert; they stand a few steps apart at the doorway.
